stem: Under the 1987 Constitution, which two officials must be at least forty years old?
choices: The President and a Member of the Supreme Court
A Senator and a Member of the Supreme Court
A Senator and a Member of the House of Representatives
answer: The President and a Member of the Supreme Court
hints: Recall the minimum age for each office in the choices: the President, a Senator, a Member of the House and a Member of the Supreme Court.
Find the ages in Article VI, Section 3 (Senator), Article VI, Section 6 (House), Article VII, Section 2 (President) and Article VIII, Section 7 (Supreme Court).
Write each office's minimum age next to it. Then pick the pair where both ages are forty.

solution.methodName: Line up the ages and terms by office

steps.action: President: "at least forty years of age on the day of the election" (Article VII, Section 2).
Member of the Supreme Court: "must be at least forty years of age" (Article VIII, Section 7).
steps.why: Members of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President (Article VIII, Section 9), not elected, so their age is not tied to an election day.

steps.action: Senator: "at least thirty-five years of age" (Article VI, Section 3). Member of the House: "at least twenty-five years of age" (Article VI, Section 6).
Line them up: President 40, Supreme Court 40, Senator 35, House 25.
The President and a Member of the Supreme Court must be at least forty years old.

trapNotes.The President and a Senator: The President must be at least 40, but a Senator needs to be only at least 35 (Article VI, Section 3).
trapNotes.A Senator and a Member of the Supreme Co: A Member of the Supreme Court must be at least 40, but a Senator needs to be only at least 35.
trapNotes.A Senator and a Member of the House of R: Neither needs to be 40. A Senator must be at least 35 and a Member of the House at least 25.

sourceRef.citation: 1987 Constitution, Article VI, Sections 3 and 6; Article VII, Section 2; Article VIII, Section 7
